name: BASS
fuels: PMMA slabs, cylinders and spheres; SIBAL cotton‑fiberglass fabric; Nomex, Ultem
meas: Color video, flame spread rate, extinction by flow and by N₂ suppressant jet
finding: Concurrent flame growth over fabric at 21% O₂ and 5–19 cm/s airflow; flames were most sensitive to flow at the lowest speeds.
earth: Informs flame‑spread models used for materials screening.

tests.varied: Airflow: 5, 10, 11 and 19 cm/s; sample material and geometry (flat, cylinder, sphere)

equipment: Nitrogen jet suppression of burning solids
data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: BASS‑II
full: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
fuels: PMMA, cotton‑fiberglass fabric and other thin solids
meas: Video, flame spread, flammability limits at reduced O₂
finding: PSI‑25 experimental table: 130 ISS tests by six PI teams on PMMA films, rods and slabs, SIBAL fabric, Nomex and wax, at 13.6–22.2% initial O₂. Materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity than in normal gravity; flames shrank to flamelets at low flow, blew off at high flow, and always quenched when the fan was turned off (Olson et al., ICES 2019).
earth: Extends limiting‑oxygen data used in material selection.

tests.varied: O₂ lowered by N₂ dilution; airflow from near 0 up to about 53 cm/s

equipment: Nitrogen jet suppression of burning solids
Ventilation shutdown during fire response (tested conditions)
data_status: Test‑level values from the PSI experimental table

name: Saffire‑I
fuels: SIBAL fabric (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass), 0.4 × 0.95 m
meas: Video, radiometers, thermocouples, cabin O₂ and CO₂ change
finding: First large‑scale fire in a spacecraft‑sized volume; shows how a realistic fire grows and loads the cabin atmosphere.
equipment: Cabin O₂ / CO₂ change as an early fire signature
data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: Saffire‑II
fuels: Nine 5 × 29 cm samples: silicone (3 thicknesses), SIBAL, PMMA, PMMA‑to‑Nomex transition, structured PMMA
meas: Ignition and flammability of spacecraft materials, video, cabin gas sensors
finding: Compared ignition and burning of real spacecraft materials side by side in one microgravity atmosphere.

tests.varied: Nine materials and thicknesses: silicone ×3, SIBAL, PMMA, PMMA‑to‑Nomex, structured PMMA; flow 20 cm/s (one sample at 30 cm/s)

data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: Saffire‑III
fuels: SIBAL fabric, 0.4 × 0.95 m
meas: Video, radiometers, cabin O₂ and CO₂ change
finding: Repeat large‑scale burn that confirms Saffire‑I trends and adds flow‑direction data.
equipment: Cabin O₂ / CO₂ change as an early fire signature
data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: Saffire‑IV–VI
full: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiments IV–VI (verify PSI availability)
fuels: Spacecraft solid materials at exploration atmospheres (see ICES‑2024 paper)
meas: Flame spread, flammability, cabin gas and smoke sensors
finding: Large‑scale burns at 22% O₂ / 100 kPa, 26.2% / 70.7 kPa and about 29–31% / 54–55 kPa: the only spacecraft‑scale solid fire data near lunar habitat oxygen levels.
data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: SAME
fuels: Overheated (non‑flaming) Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose, dibutyl phthalate
meas: Particle size distribution, commercial and spacecraft smoke detectors
finding: Smoke particles in microgravity can be larger than on Earth, which changes which detector types respond.
earth: Fed improvements in terrestrial smoke detection.

tests.varied: Material heated (Teflon, Kapton, silicone, cellulose, dibutyl phthalate) and heating temperature

equipment: Smoke detectors sized for larger microgravity smoke particles
False‑alarm rejection against cabin and lunar dust
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: SAME‑R
full: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment – Reflight
fuels: Overheated Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber, Pyrell foam
meas: Particle size distribution, detector response
finding: Refines smoke particle data for next‑generation spacecraft detector design.

tests.varied: Material heated (Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone, Pyrell)

equipment: Smoke detectors sized for larger microgravity smoke particles
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: DAFT / DAFT‑2
full: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
fuels: No fuel; ambient cabin dust
meas: Particle counter shared with SAME smoke tests
finding: Baseline cabin dust levels, needed to keep smoke detectors from false alarms; relevant to lunar dust.
equipment: False‑alarm rejection against cabin and lunar dust
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: FLEX
fuels: Heptane and methanol droplets
meas: Droplet burning rate, flame extinction, CO₂ and He diluent effects
finding: Limiting oxygen index ≈ 0.12 for methanol and ≈ 0.15 for heptane droplets; CO₂ and helium dilution extinguish flames, and heptane showed long‑lived cool flames after visible extinction.

tests.varied: Fuel (heptane, methanol); O₂ mole fraction 0.1–0.4; pressure 0.7–3 atm; CO₂ or He diluent
tests.fixed: Free droplets in the MDCA, quiescent

equipment: Post‑extinction monitoring for cool flames and re‑ignition
data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: FLEX‑2
fuels: Multicomponent fuel droplets, droplet arrays
meas: Burning rate, soot, flame spread between droplets
finding: Fire spread along droplet arrays and soot behaviour of fuel blends.
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: CFI
fuels: n‑alkane droplets
meas: Cool flame lifetime and chemistry
finding: Low‑temperature cool flames persist where hot flames go out, a hidden hazard for re‑ignition.
equipment: Post‑extinction monitoring for cool flames and re‑ignition
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: ACME · BRE
fuels: Gaseous fuel through a porous burner, emulating burning solids and liquids
meas: Heat flux, burning rate as a function of material properties
finding: In still air, emulated fuels self‑extinguished below about 25% O₂ but burned for minutes at elevated oxygen: oxygen‑rich habitats remove the quiescent safety margin.

tests.varied: Ambient O₂ and emulated material properties
tests.fixed: Quiescent atmosphere; flames self‑extinguished below ~25% O₂

data_status: Reported in NASA technical reports

name: ACME · CFI‑G
fuels: Propane/N₂ ambient, O₂/N₂ flowing from spherical burner (inside‑out flame)
meas: Flame structure, cool flame limits
finding: Highest oxygen concentrations tested in microgravity (up to 85%), the only PSI data near suit and high‑O₂ habitat conditions.
data_status: Stated in the Space Apps challenge brief

name: ACME · E‑FIELD
full: Electric‑Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
fuels: Gaseous jet flames under applied electric field
meas: Flame shape and ion current under field
finding: An electric field acts on flame ions to reproduce some body‑force effects; a partial analogue for gravity, not a substitute for partial‑gravity tests.
data_status: Stated in the Space Apps challenge brief

name: ACME · CLD Flame
fuels: Gaseous fuel jet in coflowing air
meas: Soot volume fraction, temperature
finding: Soot formation without buoyancy, the source of smoke that detectors must see.

tests.varied: Matched fuel and coflow velocity: 10, 20, 30 and 40 cm/s

data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: ACME · Flame Design
fuels: Spherical diffusion flames
meas: Soot inception and oxidation
finding: Shows how flame chemistry controls whether a fire is sooty or clean.
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: ACME · s‑Flame
full: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
fuels: Spherical burner, gaseous fuels
meas: Flame growth, extinction
finding: Validates models that predict when a quiescent flame grows or dies.
data_status: Estimated envelope, not yet checked against PSI

name: SPICE
fuels: Gaseous fuel jets
meas: Smoke point, soot emission
finding: Determines when a flame starts emitting smoke in microgravity; built the duct later reused by BASS and SLICE.
data_status: Stated in the Space Apps challenge brief

name: SLICE
fuels: Gaseous fuel jets
meas: Flame liftoff and blowout
finding: Airflow speeds at which a flame lifts off and blows out without buoyancy.
data_status: Stated in the Space Apps challenge brief
